codebot-demo.caption: Simulated codebot: scoped plan approval, a pull request, and a fresh approval for a new repository.

hubspot-companies-demo.caption: Simulated HubSpot agent: a scheduled company digest and owner-approved contact sharing.

reviewbot-demo.caption: Simulated reviewbot: a pull-request-triggered, read-only review summarized in Slack and recorded as a Check Run.

pm-agent-demo.caption: Simulated pm-bot: read-only GitHub and Linear work summarized against product goals.

multiplayer-approval.caption: A multiplayer session with two owner gates: approving Alex to take part, then approving the production deploy.

mp-join.caption: A new participant is gated: srebot waits for an owner to approve Alex before acting on his message.

mp-dm.caption: The production-deploy approval, DMed to an owner so they can approve without opening the channel.

mp-complete.caption: Once an owner approves, the card resolves in place and srebot completes the rollout.

codebot-plangate.caption: codebot proposes a plan to open a PR on acme/widget; one approval covers the plan and slots that repo.

cb-plan.caption: The plan-gate approval card: each phase and the blast radius of its permissions — read, write, and the external step that opens the PR.

cb-run.caption: Approved in one click; the steps inside the plan then run without prompting again, ending in an opened PR.

cb-scope.caption: The approval was slotted to acme/widget — a different repo needs a fresh one.

shared-permissions.caption: Sam asks for Circldot's contacts; the approval routes to Circldot's owner (Jordan), who approves before the data is shared.

sp-dm.caption: The approval is DMed to the company's owner — not to whoever asked — with what's being shared, why, and the permission it grants.

sp-return.caption: Only after the owner approves does the agent return the contacts to the requester.

identity-choice.caption: codebot asks whose identity to use; a recommender suggests "Run as me", Jordan confirms, and the work runs under Jordan's account.

id-badges.caption: Every agent shows which identity it uses: "Uses YOUR account" (passthrough) vs. "Uses an operator account" (agent identity).

id-prompt.caption: The per-session identity choice: run as the agent, run as me, or cancel — with dynamic's advisory suggestion highlighted.

id-chosen.caption: Once you choose, the session resolves and the agent proceeds under that identity.

web-signin.caption: The local web UI is gated by the admin password you set at install.

web-newsession.caption: Starting a session from the browser: pick an agent, say what you need.

web-chat.caption: A pirate-speak agent answering in the browser chat — the same session surface the Desktop “New chat…” opens.

agent-definition-demo.caption: One reviewable class, two independent sessions — each with its own scope, budget, and audit trail.

agent-definition-sessions.caption: The same class running as two separate sessions, one per thread.

safe-tools-demo.caption: Read-only steps run freely; the external deploy asks for approval first, then runs in a locked-down sandbox.

safe-tools-approval.caption: An external tool call, approved — the card is computed from the call: the exact deploy and its blast radius.

channels-demo.caption: Reached with an @mention in a real thread; the App Home tab is the agent's at-a-glance hub.

channels-apphome.caption: The App Home hub: what the agent is, whose account it acts as, and which services it's connected to.

memory-demo.caption: The agent recalls from an authorized store, then produces and delivers a durable, versioned artifact.

memory-artifact.caption: A durable, versioned artifact delivered in-thread — attached to the reply, and rendered inert.

egress-leakage.caption: The information-leakage gate: a reply would reach a guest who can't see the data, so the data owner is asked to approve the share.

mid-turn-queue.caption: A message sent mid-turn is queued, not dropped — with a one-click “Interrupt & Send Now”.

artifacts-demo.caption: A durable artifact is delivered, then revised in place — a new immutable revision advances `latest` while the link keeps pointing at the report.

artifact-viewer.caption: Annotating the rendered artifact in the viewer: mark up an element, leave a note, and send the batch back to the agent to revise.

thread-adoption.caption: @-mentioned into an existing thread, the bot adopts it — the prior discussion is now its context, and the people in it (sam, riley) are participants who can talk to it and approve what it does.

console-init.caption: `oap init --local`, scripted end to end: resolve the kind → build → install (live checklist) → seed authorization → health-check → first-run setup.

console-check.caption: `oap check` — each component reports for itself: ✓ healthy, ⚠ degraded, ✗ down.

admin-tour.caption: A walkthrough of the real admin dashboard — Overview, live sessions, approvals, the agent config, tiered settings, and the audit log.

admin-agents.caption: Config › Agents — every AgentClass and its readiness; installing an agent from here is a permissioned action too.

admin-settings.caption: Config › Settings — the tiered defaults and ceilings, resolved and shown per setting.

desktop-settings.caption: Desktop → Settings → Cluster — the model catalog, limits and defaults as sub-tabs, validated against the live cluster before you save.

admin-logs.caption: Audit › Logs — the cross-session, tamper-evident record: lifecycle events, tool calls, and authorization decisions.

admin-sessions.caption: Sessions — every agent session, current and historical, with status and estimated tokens.

admin-toolcalls.caption: Live tool calls — tool invocations as they happen, across every session.

admin-approvals.caption: Approvals — tool calls and leakage gates awaiting a human decision.

admin-channels.caption: Channels — where agents are reachable, and each binding's connection status.

admin-directory.caption: Directory — the directory syncs feeding SpiceDB (Slack, GitHub, 1Password memberships).

admin-identity.caption: Identity — agent identities, their credentials, and the login providers people sign in through.

admin-memory.caption: Memory — the searchable, authorized memory store: kinds, entry counts, and scopes.

admin-artifacts.caption: Artifacts — the durable, versioned outputs agents have produced.

admin-budget.caption: Budget — estimated spend by model, agent, session, and user.

builder-first-agent.caption: One build, end to end: describe the agent, answer its questions, approve the stage once, test it live on the page, and keep the draft.

builder-newsession.caption: The session picker lists Agent Builder for the people named at install; the message can stay empty.

builder-intake.caption: The workshop page opens on Intake with one form: what should this agent do?

builder-questions.caption: The builder restates what it understood, lists what is settled, and asks one question at a time.

builder-approve-card.caption: The stage card in the conversation view: approve it once and every change in that stage runs without another card.

builder-test.caption: Test: a real session of the new agent embedded on the page, with the builder watching what it does.

builder-deliver.caption: Deliver: a saved copy of exactly what was tested, and three choices — install for real, hand the draft to someone, test again.

builder-install-requested.caption: Install for real records a request for a platform admin; nothing runs until they approve it.

admin-workshops.caption: The admin console lists every open workshop — who started it, its phase, and any install request waiting on it.

admin-workshops-install.caption: Install asks for the namespace the agent should land in, plus any install-time questions the draft declares.

admin-workshops-installed.caption: Installed: the row records where the agent landed; the person who asked is told.

builder-permissions.caption: Permissions, in the person's words: what the agent will do on its own, what it will ask about first, and what it will never do.
